Subject: Scaling probe & commitment orchestration

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput numbers looked promising. We want to validate performance before our finance commit. Proposed ask: a 72-hour scaling probe that mirrors ~300 qps peak for our text-generation route, then a small staged cutover to reserved capacity.

Key constraints:
- Data residency: must run in us-west region only.
- Warm cache behavior: we rely heavily on prefix caching; need to understand KV cache warmup time and steady-state token cost.
- SLA ask: finance wants a backup plan so we can fall back to hosted API during the first 2 weeks without penalty.

Can you outline a lightweight probe + acceptance criteria and a cutover cadence we can share with procurement? Procurement will want timelines and any DocuSign/PO requirements.

Cheers,
Evan
---

Evan — great to hear. Quick draft plan below; attaching a simple probe-matrix (redwood-probe-matrix.xlsx) with knobs we typically run.

Summary plan (72h probe + staged swap):
1) Probe prep (Day 0): baseline traffic capture, deploy mirrored traffic to a dedicated probe pool (single AZ us-west) for 24h to validate perf.
2) Steady probe (Day 1-3): ramp to target 300 qps peak across representative prompts, exercise cold-to-warm KV cache transitions. Capture tail latency, token cost, and mem/GPU utilization.
3) Acceptance gate (end Day 3):
   - P95 latency <= 240ms at target load
   - Token cost within 10% of hosted estimate in probe matrix
   - No OOMs or sustained GPU GC events
4) Canary swap (Day 4-5): 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% on Dedicated with 30m hold windows and automatic rollback on SLA triggers.

Rollback triggers (examples): sustained P95 > 350ms for 10m, >2% error rate, or token-cost delta >20% unexplainable by prompt mix.

SLA fallback: we can include a 14-day grace period where requests route back to hosted without overage penalty; we document fallback routing and billing treatment in the mutual-action plan. Procurement items: draft SOW, PO amount tied to committed vGPU-hours, and DocuSign for the reserved capacity addendum.

Karthik/Ben — can you confirm the probe pool sizing and estimated GPU-hours for 300 qps? Evan — if these acceptance gates look ok I’ll loop in Monica (CS) to draft the MPA and a cutover calendar for your team.

—Marissa

Thanks, Marissa — that plan is aligned with what our CTO asked for. Two clarifications:
1) For the probe pool, can you confirm whether caching is warm-started from a 24h mirror or if we should expect a full cold start? Our traffic pattern has a lot of repeat prefixes and we'd prefer warm-start.
2) Procurement wants an outline of the DocuSign items and whether the grace fallback needs a separate credit line or if it's covered under the reserved commitment.

We approve moving forward with probe scheduling tentatively the week of Jun 21 — want to lock dates if your team has capacity.

—Evan

Evan — answering inline and attaching a short mutual-action-plan PDF (edgeops-mutual-action-plan.pdf) for procurement.

> can you confirm whether caching is warm-started from a 24h mirror or if we should expect a full cold start?
We can warm-seed the KV cache using a 24h mirrored traffic snapshot (recommended). The probe-matrix includes warm vs cold cost deltas we typically see; with warm-seeding you should expect a 15-25% lower token cost during the steady probe. We’ll run the mirror for 12–24h prior to the steady probe phase to populate hot prefixes.

> does the grace fallback need separate credit line?
The fallback is handled as a short-term routing policy: during the 14-day grace period traffic routed back to hosted will be billed at the hosted rate but we’ll apply a prepaid credit equivalent to X% of committed spend (outlined in the MPA). Procurement: see page 2 of the attached MPA for DocuSign checklist (SLA addendum, reserved capacity terms, PO instructions).

Probe sizing note (Karthik/Ben): for 300 qps peak with 8–12 token average response, we recommend staging on 6 x A100-80GB equiv GPUs for the probe pool (shared batchers, continuous KV caching enabled). Estimated GPU-hours for the 72h steady probe ~ 432 GPU-hours; can you confirm we have a slot the week of Jun 21?

Next steps:
- Marissa to schedule probe window (tentative Jun 21–24) and send calendar invites.
- Karthik/Ben to provision probe pool and confirm resource reservation.
- Monica to finalize MPA and DocuSign packet and share with procurement.

If procurement needs a formal SOW line-item for the warm-seeding work we can add it as an optional task.

Thanks — I’ll slot time with Monica and Evan for Wednesday to run through the MPA checklist.

—Marissa

Onward,
